summary:
IT HOLDS. Round 13, and I re-attacked both repairs rather than reading the summary of them.

NO ASSERTION WEAKENED, checked first and independently of the repairs. `format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java` is still the only staged file under a test path. Its diff touches the class javadoc and the text inside one `.as(...)` description; `.contains("byteStart=4096")` and `.contains("byteLen=65536")` appear as CONTEXT lines, byte-identical, as do the round-trip predicates at lines 81-82 (`byteStart()` isZero, `byteLen()` isEqualTo 4_096) and the paired-absence refusals at 96-99. Eighth round running. And the only `src/main` file staged is `SubscriptionEvent.java`, whose 34 added lines are every one of them a javadoc `*` line -- I filtered the diff for non-comment content and it is empty -- so no production logic changed and no new test is owed. I did not run the suite; the 1281/0 baseline is the parent's claim, not mine. What I own is the non-weakening check and it passes on the bytes.

REPAIR 1 LANDED AND NOTHING ELSE ENDORSES THE RETIRED WORDING. `grep -c 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION'` over the staged backlog returns 0, and a wider grep for `constant in K` / `CONSTANT-IN-K` across every `.md` and `.java` in the tree returns exactly two hits: M5.45h's own MARKED retraction ("AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS CLAUSE SAID 'CONSTANT IN K' ... WHICH IS WEAKER THAN THE LITERAL IT REPLACED") and the chronological round-10 paragraph in `review/overrides.md`, which the round-11 and round-12 paragraphs of the SAME entry explicitly retract two and three paragraphs later. A round-by-round narrative that says what round 10 did and what round 11 found wrong with it is not an unmarked live endorsement, and it is not a document M5.66's owner builds from. I am naming it here so it is not re-derived rather than raising it. What remains in M5.45h criterion 1 is the binding form alone -- at most one `fetchDirectory` and at most one `fetchRange` invocation per (node, segment) -- and I re-checked it still reds the survivor the deletion was made for: the `(segmentKey, indexId)` cache reports 2 `fetchRange` invocations against at most one, RED, where a constancy assertion at two shares read 2 and 2 and passed.

REPAIR 2 LANDED AND I VERIFIED IT SYMBOLICALLY, NOT JUST ON THE WORKED NUMBERS. The clause now names **K = crossover with DOUBLED runs** (1,772,134 > 886,067) and **K = crossover + 1 with HALVED runs** (445,570 <= 886,067). The arithmetic checks: 169 * 10,486 = 1,772,134 and 170 * 2,621 = 445,570 against a budget of 169 * 5,243 = 886,067. More importantly the pair is parameterised by whatever crossover the owner RECORDS, not by 169, so I re-derived it for a general C: doubled runs give sum = 2*C*r > C*r for every C, so the proxy goes whole-object where the truth is bounded; halved runs give (C+1)*r/2 <= C*r for every C >= 1, so it goes bounded where the truth is whole-object. Both sides red at any recorded crossover, which is what makes the named pair a rule rather than an instance. The two-sided relation now sits in the same clause and supplies the DIRECTION the pair needs -- exactly two requests and fewer bytes at K = crossover, exactly one request and exactly the whole-object bytes at K = crossover + 1 -- so an owner building only the second fixture still reds the `nodeRunCount <= 1` mutant the primary pair was written for.

I ALSO CHECKED THE NEW CASES ARE SATISFIABLE, because a criterion that reds its own intended implementation is this row's own recorded failure mode. Under both readings of "doubled runs" -- 1,600 runs in a 16 MiB object, or 800 runs in the same 8 MiB -- the bounded path at K = crossover fetches header + span (78,400 + 16,579,830 = 16,658,230 of 16,777,216; or 39,200 + 8,289,919 = 8,329,119 of 8,388,608), strictly fewer than the whole object in both, so "fewer bytes" is reachable and the ambiguity between the two readings does not change what is falsified. The halved fixture at K = crossover + 1 takes the whole-object path and carries no byte relation to strain.

ONE MORE SURVIVOR CLASS I TESTED AGAINST THE FINISHED CELL, since the boundary-only argument invites it: a SPAN-RATIO proxy (`span/objLen <= f(crossover)`) is invisible to both new fixtures, because at a fixed K the interleaved span ratio (K-1)/(K+1) is the same whatever the run size. It is killed elsewhere and I confirmed where: the K = 2 case at the segment's extremes has a span ratio of ~1, so the proxy takes whole-object and issues one request where (i) demands two. The invariant set closes it without another fixture.

NOTHING TO RAISE. Two edits, both pure and both in the direction this row's own record says has never regressed -- one deletion and one naming of cases already derived in review. I found no defect that would change what M5.66's owner builds or would let a wrong implementation pass, and after twelve rounds I would rather record that plainly than manufacture a thirteenth.
